clue.text: Frantic SOS: "Save species!" (Mine and yours exemplified here!)

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so the letters of the quoted plea are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A panicky conservationist cries SOS, begging for an endangered species to be saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantic' rearranges SOS, SAVE and SPECIES, fourteen letters in all. The parenthesis defines by example: 'mine' and 'yours' are possessive pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: possessive forms such as mine and yours show ownership, so they illustrate this grammatical category.

clue.text: Certain qualification needed in English, comparatively speaking!

parts.note: to be certain is to be positive
a degree is an academic qualification

explanation.surface: An applicant needs a definite qualification in English, the advert says with a hint of comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar an adjective's comparison runs through three degrees, e.g. big, bigger, biggest; the plain form is the first of them, hence 'comparatively speaking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical term: the uninflected form of an adjective or adverb, before comparative and superlative, in English grammar.

clue.text: A raspberry is defined thus initially, so you never call a raspberry "plum"

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word from 'so' through to 'plum'

explanation.surface: A pedant insists a raspberry must never be called a plum, given its botanical definition.
explanation.walkthrough: A raspberry is a compound fruit formed from many fused carpels, which is what the botanical term means.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term: a raspberry is an aggregate fruit made of united carpels, which is exactly this kind of fruit.

clue.text: Hire-purchase with messy rate fluctuation

indicators.note: fluctuation is shifting and changing, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a hire-purchase deal comes with an unstable, messy interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuation' rearranges MESSY and RATE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in instalments over time, as in British hire-purchase, is buying on generous credit arrangements.

clue.text: Smell a rat, as usual, in Captain Renault's round-up

definitions.meaning: to smell a rat is to have a suspicion, a verb sense

definitions.text: as usual, in Captain Renault's round-up
definitions.meaning: in the film Casablanca, Captain Renault orders his men to round up the usual ones, a noun sense

explanation.surface: Someone senses foul play, just as a policeman in an old film habitually arrests the usual people.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Renault, the French police chief in Casablanca, famously says 'Round up the usual suspects.'
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to sense wrongdoing; a suspect is a person rounded up by police as possibly guilty.

clue.text: "Taxi Driver" is mostly expressing life as art in music

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, so the letters are pressed out of the run of words

explanation.surface: A film critic claims the movie Taxi Driver largely portrays life as artistic realism set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi' is surface only; the run sits across 'driVER IS MOstly'. The term names the Italian realist school of opera (Mascagni, Leoncavallo).
explanation.definitionFit: Realism in opera: this movement portrayed everyday, often sordid life on the musical stage.

clue.text: Fancy name I see, but no supporter of Diogenes

indicators.note: no here means without, so the following synonym is taken out of the first word

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
C sounds like 'see' and is a crossword convention for it

explanation.surface: Someone with a grand name says they will see the ancient philosopher but not back him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes FAN from FANCY leaving CY. Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous member of the Cynic school.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope is the classic example of a member of the ancient Greek philosophical school of Cynics.

clue.text: Pores over a time atoms reacted

indicators.note: reacted suggests a chemical change, so the letters are recombined

explanation.surface: A chemist pores over a moment when atoms underwent a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pores' reads as the verb to study closely, but it is the plural noun. 'reacted' rearranges A, T and ATOMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: the tiny pores in a leaf's surface through which gases pass are called by this plural name.

clue.text: Quotes from a thousand naïve Democrats without a turn

indicators.note: a turn here is a change of order, so the letters are rearranged once the A is left out

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Remarks quoted from a thousand innocent Democrats who never change their position.
explanation.walkthrough: M with NAIVE and DEMOCRATS gives fifteen letters; 'without' a removes one A, and 'turn' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are commonly called quotes, the usual informal name for these punctuation marks.

clue.text: Grammatical form for the meaning of society is Ney's problem

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Ney with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A historian notes that a particular grammatical construction gave Marshal Ney trouble in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges IS and NEYS; Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: a construction that follows sense rather than strict syntax, as in 'the crowd were cheering'.

clue.text: Managed Spike Milligan's converted capital?

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran
Spike Milligan was one of the Goons of the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show

explanation.surface: A question whether Spike Milligan managed to convert a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s British radio comedy starring Milligan. The city has been renamed Yangon and has lost its status as Myanmar's capital, hence 'converted'.
explanation.definitionFit: This former capital of Burma has since been renamed and replaced as capital, so it is a changed capital.

clue.text: Circular field

definitions.meaning: a circular is a leaflet handed out widely, like a short pamphlet
a field or expanse of land, as in an area of farmland

explanation.definitionFit: A short pamphlet is a circular; an extent of land such as a field is likewise a region of ground.

clue.text: Following sex change, preserve queen in ice that's dry

indicators.note: a change of the word sex rearranges its letters
in places the female cat inside the frozen word

parts.note: taken as written
a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: After gender reassignment, someone keeps a queen frozen in ice that is dry.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, a convention worth knowing. 'Following' and 'preserve' only dress the surface; 'change' rearranges, giving EXS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare verb from Latin exsiccare, meaning to drain of moisture, like desiccate.

clue.text: Salute a stop for this poor vet at dissection

indicators.note: dissection cuts things apart, so the letters are taken to pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a poor veterinary surgeon at a dissection, with a salute thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Salute (Santa Maria della Salute) is a stop on Venice's Grand Canal waterbus route, so 'Salute' is not a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian waterbus calls at the Salute church landing, so Salute is one of its stops.

clue.text: Payment avoided by some Brooklyn Dodgers?

definitions.meaning: a banker's order or cheque used for payment
military conscription, which dodgers evaded, read via the baseball team name

explanation.definitionFit: A banker's order is a form of payment; conscription in the US was evaded by so-called dodgers.

clue.text: Impresario who bid for Stravinsky; I hid gavel unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An auctioneer hid the gavel at a bad moment as an impresario bid for a Stravinsky lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges I HID GAVEL. 'bid for' means commissioned: the Ballets Russes founder commissioned The Firebird and The Rite of Spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei, founder of the Ballets Russes, was the impresario who commissioned Stravinsky's early ballets.

clue.text: Nobleman detailed as composer of "The French Harry Potter"

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a duke is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A nobleman, cut down to size, poses as the composer of a French boy-wizard story.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Dukas wrote The Sorcerer's Apprentice, a French tale of a young wizard, hence the playful Harry Potter comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul, the French composer of The Sorcerer's Apprentice, a story of a young magic student.

clue.text: Beg wildly to enter stink over CAMRA's bête noire?

indicators.note: to enter puts the jumbled word inside the reversed one
over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to reek is to stink

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of beg are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone begs frantically amid a stench, over a drink real-ale campaigners detest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means read upwards, giving KEER; 'wildly' gives GBE. CAMRA is Britain's Campaign for Real Ale, which champions cask beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressurised, filtered draught drink is what the British real-ale campaign group has long opposed.

clue.text: Coming straight to the point, outside of Ms Fitz-gerald, I'm married

indicators.note: outside of puts the married word around the other pieces

parts.note: married means wed
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer
I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Getting straight to the point, someone announces they are married, beyond Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Fitz-gerald' is the setter's spelling of the jazz singer's surname; the comma is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accurately directed shot heads straight for its target, so it is precisely directed.

clue.text: He worked with steam and water to become a painter

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: An engineer who worked with steam and water ends up as a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine, French Rococo painter famous for fêtes galantes such as Pilgrimage to Cythera.

clue.text: Ideal place for a Callas performance?

definitions.text: Ideal place for a Callas performance?

indicators.note: a performance can be a fuss or a display, signalling the letters are worked over

explanation.surface: The perfect venue for the soprano Maria Callas to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges A CALLAS, and the whole clue describes the Milan opera house where Callas famously sang.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's great opera house was the venue of Maria Callas's greatest triumphs.

clue.text: Spoil the ship, left off the tar!

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: a liner is a ship

explanation.surface: An echo of the saying about spoiling the ship for a ha'porth of tar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface twists the proverb 'spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar'. 'tar' is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar is old slang for a sailor or seaman.

clue.text: Lots of storage needed when Ms Roslin moves into French accommodation

indicators.note: moves into puts the presenter inside the French lodgings

parts.note: gîtes are French holiday cottages
Gaby Roslin, the British TV presenter

explanation.surface: A computer needs plenty of storage when a TV presenter moves into a French cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaby Roslin is a British TV and radio presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each unit is a billion bytes, so many of them amount to a large quantity of computer memory.

clue.text: Naked force used to invade vessel

indicators.note: used to invade puts the force letter inside the other word

parts.note: naked means bare
G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Raw power is deployed to storm a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Black icon rejected Marx

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey, the American talk-show host

explanation.surface: A Black icon dismisses the ideas of Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl, but it is one of the Marx Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent, harp-playing member of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Old dear disturbed English discussion groups held here

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: disturbed means upset or jumbled, so the letters of dear are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly lady was upset in English discussion groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old dear' reads as an elderly woman but splits into two jobs; 'disturbed' gives EDRA. The word is the Latin plural of exedra.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical architecture: these recesses or halls with seating were places for conversation.

clue.text: So Gordius to his setter: "Put the lot on Bunthorne's retirement"

parts.note: all means the lot

indicators.note: retirement means drawing back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the setter Bunthorne speaking of himself, so 'my'

explanation.surface: Gordius, a fellow setter, urges Bunthorne to stake everything on his retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link. Gordius is another Guardian setter's pen-name, so it stands to the man behind it as a borrowed name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-name taken from another person's real name, as a setter's pseudonym stands for him.

clue.text: Words of action from the Baker Street enthusiasts?

definitions.text: Words of action from the Baker Street enthusiasts?

parts.words: Words of action from the Baker Street enthusiasts?
parts.note: verbs are action words, and a Sherlock Holmes fan society is named after Holmes's street-boy helpers

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: action words with non-standard forms, punning on the Sherlock Holmes society.
